extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: The largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing about two trillion tokens of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data across a wide variety of languages and domains.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: PleIAs (Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov)
extraction.inLanguage: en, fr, de, es, la, it, pl, el, pt, ru
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Aggregation of open datasets, public domain texts, open source code, and semantic data from various sources into six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data comes from various open sources including SEC, WTO, AMF, TED EU Tenders, GATT Library, Europarl, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, USPTO, UN Digital Library, OECD, Chronicling America, Europeana, Gallica, Biblioteca, OpenAlex, ArXiv, The Stack v1 and v2, Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is replaced with fictitious but realistic values. Documents containing harmful language are either removed or synthetically rewritten without the harmful language. Additionally, for highly deteriorated content with OCR errors, the OCRonos model acts as a synthetic rewriting tool to provide sensible restitution of the deteriorated text.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PII is replaced with fictitious but realistic values. Toxic content is either removed or synthetically rewritten. Wikidata items and properties are translated into simple natural language sequences.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation using Segmentext, OCR error detection using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr, OCR correction using OCRonos, PII removal using Presidio, toxicity filtering using Celadon, and code filtering (removing specific file extensions, non-permissive licenses, and files with >=75% digits).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is an evolving resource with past versions archived on HuggingFace for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to support the pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs by making it legal to release the source without relying on fair use, while mitigating potential biases and harms.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical texts may contain harmful language and biases, including race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Does not cover the entire range of available open data, shallow coverage for low-resource languages, not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning, and curation methods do not have 100% accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training Large Language Models, developing vision-language models (VLMs), historical language models, and creating ethical fine-tuning datasets.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Many texts there are historical periodicals and monographs from at least 80 years ago. Cultural norms surrounding the discussion of certain ethnic groups, women, and themes such as violence have changed dramatically. ... Celadon identifies toxic and harmful content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data, which we call the open data paradox ... the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. ... Common Corpus naturally does not contain data for instruction-tuning and any forms of specialized tasks. Therefore, it is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning. ... none of the curation methods could naturally facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy.
